title: One generic analyze_document tool versus a few non-overlapping tools
exam_question: What redesign best improves tool selection and downstream reliability without creating unnecessary tool sprawl?
correct_option_text: Replace analyze_document with a few non-overlapping tools for distinct workflows, each with clear descriptions, JSON Schema inputs, and minimal stable result fields.
why: Descriptions and input_schema are what drive tool selection. One catch-all tool hides incompatible workflows behind an operation parameter; one tool per field creates sprawl. A few purpose-specific tools with strong contracts (extract, summarise, verify against a source excerpt) give Claude a clean choice and give the validator a stable payload. strict: true keeps the input schema-conformant; semantic validation is still yours.
rubric: Learner can name the three workflows that were hiding behind the operation parameter and explain why they do not overlap.
Learner points to the description text that says when NOT to use each tool.
Learner explains why a schema-valid extract_invoice payload still needs the semantic total check.
task: Run the same seven documents twice: first with a single analyze_document tool (operation enum extract|summarize|verify), then with three non-overlapping tools (extract_invoice, summarize_document, verify_claim_against_source). Count how often the downstream validator receives extracted fields.
prompt_template:
<document>
{{document}}
</document>
Process this document for the accounts-payable pipeline. The downstream validator expects extracted invoice fields.
observation: generic tool: extraction chosen on 0/7 documents (the rest drifted to summarize/verify); split tools: extract_invoice chosen on 7/7, schema-valid payload on 7/7 (selection is solved by descriptions; validation is still yours)
